To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

HCG-beta and, particularly, AFP are important new tumor markers for malignant nonseminomous tumors of the uro-genital tract, that they are superior to CEA as markers, but that their clinical significance has not yet been clarified.

in patients with nonseminiomatous testicle tumor, simultaneous determination of HCG-beta and of AFP is superior to that of one marker only, that the sensitivity of HCG-beta is higher than that of AFP and that the sensitivity of both markers is higher than that in the case of CEA.

the determination of HCG-beta and of alpha 1-feto protein is of great importance for the diagnosis of subclinical metastases and for the clinical case control of malignant non-seminomatous testicular tumors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of new, more sensitive and specific tumor markers for urological tumors and the clarification of their clinical significance.

the following points: a) the clinical significance of CEA, AFP and HCG-beta as tumor markers in the diagnosis of tumors of the uro-genital tract, b) the prognostic value of these markers for the course of the disease, c) the significance of marker values for the therapy planning and case-control, d) the significance of the marker values for the prognosis.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the tumor marker determination should be performed only as a supplement to the clinical and histological examination and should not replace these methods.

the determination of the markers HCG-beta and/or AFP is a useful additional diagnostic method in the case of nonseminomatosis of the testicles and that it is not yet possible to give a reliable prognosis.
the tumor markers C, H and AFP are not tumor markers in the strict sense of the word.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
HCG-beta is the most important tumor marker for the demonstration of subclinical metastases in nonseminomatious testicular tumors.
the determination of HCG-beta, AFP and CEA in nonseminomatosis testicular tumor patients is a valuable addition to the methods already available for diagnosis (staging) of the disease.
the determination of HCG-beta, AFP, and CEA in the case of testicle tumors is of considerable importance for the clinical diagnosis and for the therapy planning and case-control.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the tumor markers HCG-beta and, particularly, AFP are of decisive value in the diagnosis of testicle tumors.
